label: D1 surge after a1->S2 (rare) trials, esp. unrewarded; a1-choice bias later
terms: (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S2 r") ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == D2) * last_is("a1 S2 u") ;; (phase == D2) * (action == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1)
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 38 sits near -0.8 and its magnitude is driven mainly by the previous trial at D1: after a1 -> S2 unrewarded (rare, unrewarded) it jumps by about +1.6 (to near +0.9), after a1 -> S2 rewarded by about +0.8, after a2 -> S2 unrewarded by about +0.65; other rewarded trials lower it a little. The a1 S2 u boost carries into the next D2 (+0.5). Outside D1 it is somewhat higher when the choice is a1 (D2: this trial action a1; GO: previous action a1). Value and the hidden good state add little. Observed-only 7 terms: test R^2 beyond timing 0.71 (ceiling all 0.85, all observed 0.79; last-trial table alone 0.72). A version using the upcoming GO choice (future at GO) gets 0.73 test; the observed-only version is recorded.

issues: The numbers reproduce. The recorded 7 terms score test R^2 beyond timing 0.712 (timing alone 0.06). The fitted weights match the explanation: D1 a1 S2 u +1.64, a1 S2 r +0.85, a2 S2 u +0.63, prev rewarded -0.19, D2 a1 S2 u +0.54, D2 action a1 +0.22, GO prev a1 +0.23.
The future-variable claim checks out. Swapping in (phase==GO)*(action==1) gives 0.725 against 0.712 for the observed-only version. So recording the observed version is correct.
Every term carries weight. Without the GO term the score drops to 0.677. The four D1 terms alone score 0.58.

The phrase 'other rewarded trials lower it slightly' is imprecise. The D1 residual after a2 S1 u (unrewarded) is -0.31, as low as after the rewarded trials. The misses output shows D1 after a2 S1 u is the most over-predicted cell (-0.21), and D1 after a1 S1 u is under-predicted (+0.14). The real contrast at D1 is closer to 'S1 outcomes and rewarded S2 outcomes low; a1 S1 u near baseline'.

The D1 boost after a2 S2 u is not uniform. It is concentrated on trials where that a2 choice was a switch away from a1. Adding (phase==D1)*last_is('a2 S2 u')*(tv('stay',-1)==0) gives that term +0.68 and the base term +0.57, raising test R^2 to 0.719. The worst-fit windows show D1 surges of about +0.85 after a1 S1 u followed by a2 S2 u, which the model under-predicts (-0.13 predicted).
Some steps have no previous trial in the window (prev = '?'). The model under-predicts these (D1 +0.18, GO +0.11). This is an artifact of where the window starts, not a missing explanation.

Model-internal quantities add a little: the policy logit at D2 brings the score to 0.74, and at D1 to 0.76. The remaining gap to the 0.79 observed-only ceiling is spread over many small cells. I found no single large systematic error class, and no tried term with history from two trials back added more than about 0.01.
